records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS global TCP congestion-control selector changes the congestion-avoidance algorithm from default CUBIC to model-based BBR using bottleneck bandwidth and round-trip propagation time estimates.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: A new TCP flow negotiates TCP options; FortiGate forwards/proxies data and the sender's congestion-control algorithm adjusts its sending rate as ACK/RTT and delivery-rate observations evolve. Algorithm is selected globally, not by SD-WAN rule.
records.failure_class: Throughput degradation under congestion or high bandwidth-delay product; false attribution of receive-window limitation to congestion control.
records.evidence_pattern: Compare identical transfers and path conditions with BBR and CUBIC; capture SYN/SYN-ACK window-scale negotiation separately; compare RTT, retransmissions, delivered rate and throughput. A 65,535-byte window with no scaling is not evidence of BBR failure.
records.remediation_path: Validate TCP option negotiation and policy/proxy behavior first; then set config system global set tcp-congestion-control bbr, run controlled repeatable tests, and revert to cubic if the workload/path performs worse.
records.question_fingerprint: Given equal RTT and link capacity but different congestion behavior, identify which observation distinguishes a BBR bottleneck model from a TCP receive-window cap.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two parallel TCP transfer paths through one FortiGate with a global algorithm selector, receiver ACK/RTT feedback loop, and a separate SYN-option/window-scaling diagnostic callout.

uniqueness_check.rejected_near_match: 2026-10-27 explicit-proxy TCP window-scaling failure is a TCP-option/window-size mechanism, not congestion-control selection; use only as a contrast scenario.

records.lesson_subject: FortiManager 8.0 management of multiple FortiSASE instances as managed devices
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager Device Manager treats multiple FortiSASE instances as distinct managed-device objects; onboarding authorization is based on shared FortiCare account or shared FortiCloud OU/sub-OU plus a FortiManager Key.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiSASE Central Management is enabled; FortiManager adds a FortiSASE device object; tenant identity and FortiManager Key establish the management relationship; instances can be placed in one ADOM while remaining separate SASE environments.
records.failure_class: Tenant onboarding rejected because account/OU relationships or Central Management/key prerequisites are inconsistent; accidental conflation of tenant identity with ADOM grouping.
records.evidence_pattern: Check Central Management state, FortiCare account and OU hierarchy, generated FortiManager Key, Device Manager managed-device entry, and ADOM placement. Presence in one ADOM proves centralized inventory, not that the SASE tenants share policy or data planes.
records.remediation_path: Enable Central Management with FortiCare Support if required; confirm the exact FortiCloud account/OU relationship; generate and supply a FortiManager Key only for a different account in the same OU hierarchy; add each SASE instance separately and validate its device status.
records.question_fingerprint: Three SASE instances belong to separate child OUs but share one parent organization; determine when the FortiManager Key is required and what ADOM membership does not imply.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiManager Device Manager above three isolated FortiSASE tenant clouds, with FortiCloud root/child OU trust boundary and one ADOM inventory grouping.

uniqueness_check.rejected_near_match: 2026-10-27 FortiSASE SCIM provisioning manages user lifecycle, not FortiManager-to-SASE tenant control-plane onboarding.

records.lesson_subject: FortiData incident ingestion: SIEM Xlog, siemdb insertion and event-handler boundaries
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer registers FortiData FDTxxxxxx as a supported device, ingests SIEM Xlog files, exposes raw files in Log Browse, inserts normalized incident records into siemdb, and maps Issue logs to a predefined external-alert handler.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiData sends Xlog -> FortiAnalyzer Log Browse receives raw file -> SIEM database insertion makes records queryable in Logs > All -> default handler evaluates Issue records -> Event Monitor alert; Risk Record and Integration Event require custom handlers.
records.failure_class: Raw log received but no SIEM query result or alert; incorrect assumption that all external incident types automatically trigger Event Monitor.
records.evidence_pattern: Correlate Device Manager registration, Log Browse raw file presence, Logs > All siemdb records by incident type, and Event Monitor handler output. Raw file visibility proves transport, not database insertion or alert generation.
records.remediation_path: Register the FDT device; confirm Xlog delivery and parsing; validate siemdb visibility; inspect the enabled Ingested External Alerts handler for Issue logs; create and test custom handlers for Risk Record and Integration Event.
records.question_fingerprint: A FortiData Risk Record is visible in Log Browse and Logs > All but no Event Monitor alert exists; identify the missing processing stage.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiData source branching into raw Log Browse and siemdb, then Issue-only default event handler to Event Monitor, with separate custom-handler branches for Risk Record and Integration Event.

uniqueness_check.rejected_near_match: This is not Fluentd forwarding or FortiAI triage: it is native FortiData Xlog registration, SIEM DB ingestion and incident-type-specific alert mapping.

records.lesson_subject: Auto-topology and auto-ISL lifecycle: LLDP discovery, LACP-active trunk creation and VLAN side effects
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitch auto-network discovers peer links and automatically forms one LACP-active ISL trunk per switch pair; additional physical links to the same peer are enrolled in the existing auto-ISL.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: LLDP/peer discovery identifies the adjacent switch; auto-network creates an ISL trunk and logical switch interface; management VLAN becomes native, VLANs 1-4094 are allowed, DHCP snooping is trusted, and STP edge is disabled.
records.failure_class: Manual trunk creation fails because ports are already owned by auto-ISL; unintended native VLAN or topology behavior after factory reset or zero-touch initialization.
records.evidence_pattern: show switch trunk reveals auto-isl 1 and member ports; Switch > Interfaces blue icon indicates active ISL; inspect mgmt-vlan, native VLAN, allowed VLANs, DHCP snooping and STP edge attributes.
records.remediation_path: Decide whether auto-topology is intended; set mgmt-vlan distinct from an existing SVI; use LLDP profile with auto-isl disabled on selected ports or disable auto-network and auto-fortilink-discovery; when repurposing an auto-ISL member, move the generated trunk to an unused port before creating a manual trunk.
records.question_fingerprint: A port pair rejects manual LACP membership with entry-not-found even after deleting the auto-ISL; identify the ownership state and safe transition sequence.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two FortiSwitches with two physical peer links feeding one auto-generated LACP ISL trunk, a shared management/native VLAN and explicit STP/DHCP-snooping attributes.

uniqueness_check.rejected_near_match: Auto-ISL is LLDP-driven peer discovery and automatic trunk ownership, not MCLAG peer state, EVPN DF election, or manual LACP hash/aggregator selection.

records.lesson_subject: RADIUS authentication survivability for 802.1X SSIDs: local credential-hash cache and bounded outage window
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS wireless controller locally re-authenticates previously authenticated wireless clients from a bounded RADIUS survivability cache when the RADIUS server becomes unreachable; EAP-PEAP requires the Fortinet-AS-Credential-Hash or Cisco-AVPair AS-Credential-Hash attribute.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Initial RADIUS authentication and certificate trust populate a per-SSID cache; on RADIUS outage, previously authenticated station reconnects use cached credential material until radius-auth-surviv-intv expires; after expiry the station is no longer authorized; recovered RADIUS resumes normal authentication.
records.failure_class: Wireless outage during RADIUS unavailability; false belief that survivability authenticates first-time clients or provides indefinite local RADIUS service.
records.evidence_pattern: diagnose wpa wpad radius-auth-surviv-cache <ssid> shows cached STA, expiration, VLAN, EAP type and user; wlac -d sta online proves station remains online; direct authserver test can fail while cached station reconnects successfully.
records.remediation_path: Import the RADIUS root CA and server certificate, bind them globally, configure the VAP with survivability enabled and a 3600-864000-second timeout, ensure PEAP credential-hash attribute is returned, and test outage/recovery with a previously authenticated client.
records.question_fingerprint: During a RADIUS outage an existing station reconnects but a new station cannot; identify why this is expected and which cache field controls the remaining authorization window.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAP VAP and wireless controller with RADIUS server, certificate trust, per-SSID cache, existing client reconnect path, blocked first-time client path, and timeout/recovery transitions.

uniqueness_check.rejected_near_match: This is a local cached-authentication outage mechanism, not RadSec transport, EAP method selection, or DHCP relay metadata.

records.lesson_subject: Preserve Port Names and interface-model reconciliation: switch descriptions, Resync Interfaces and model rebuild boundaries
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC 9.4 Preserve Port Names is a global or per-device control determining whether switch port names/labels are retained in the FortiNAC database or refreshed from switch interface data during a resync.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiNAC builds port display names from switch name, ifName and ifDescription; routine resync updates interface status; disabling Preserve Port Names allows descriptions to update on service restart or Resync Interfaces; chassis/stack re-index can delete/recreate interface models and affect manual port groups.
records.failure_class: Port labels or descriptions remain stale despite switch-side changes; operators confuse L2 poll with interface model retrieval or unintentionally lose port-group associations after re-indexing.
records.evidence_pattern: Compare switch ifName/ifDescr with FortiNAC Inventory Ports view; inspect global Network Device and per-device Preserve Port Names setting; verify whether Resync Interfaces ran and whether the switch port sequence changed.
records.remediation_path: Keep Preserve Port Names enabled when FortiNAC labels are authoritative; disable globally or per device only when switch-side descriptions should overwrite; run Resync Interfaces or restart services; after chassis/stack changes review port groups because re-index may recreate interface models.
records.question_fingerprint: A switch description changes but FortiNAC still shows the old label after L2 polling; determine which setting and refresh operation govern description synchronization.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Switch interface table (ifName/ifDescr) feeding FortiNAC device model and Ports view through a Preserve Port Names gate, with separate L2 status-poll and full interface-resync paths.

uniqueness_check.rejected_near_match: This focuses on interface-description ownership and model re-indexing, not endpoint MAC/IP learning or host profiling.

records.lesson_subject: RADIUS-only device support in 7.6.7: reusable configuration objects, selectors and state-based access control
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F 7.6.7+ supports devices that communicate exclusively through RADIUS without SNMP/CLI, using reusable logical-network, RADIUS-server, response-attribute, VLAN-mapping and SSO/VPN configuration objects selected by ordered selectors.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Device RADIUS Access-Request supplies identity/attributes; selector rules choose server/response/VLAN/SSO objects; state-based access-control membership/group-action rules decide registration isolation or production access; RADIUS response attributes and CoA drive enforcement.
records.failure_class: RADIUS-only device remains unmanaged or receives wrong VLAN because selector configuration, rule rank, device legacy mode, VLAN mapping or RADIUS server/response attributes are inconsistent.
records.evidence_pattern: Confirm device is 7.6.7+, Device Legacy Mode is off, RADIUS Access-Request reaches FortiNAC, selector ranks select the intended objects, VLAN 11/77 mapping is correct, and Port Changes records the applied VLAN and reason.
records.remediation_path: Create reusable logical networks and RADIUS/response/VLAN/SSO objects; add specific selectors above broad matches; configure state-based access-control rules; migrate a test device out of Legacy Mode without disabling Global Legacy Mode; verify RADIUS and VLAN behavior before scaling.
records.question_fingerprint: A cloud-managed switch sends RADIUS requests but FortiNAC cannot poll it; identify the 7.6.7 selector-based object chain and the legacy-mode migration hazard.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: RADIUS-only switch/cloud device to FortiNAC-F with ordered selector stack selecting reusable RADIUS, response, logical VLAN and SSO objects, then state-based access-control branch to Registration or Production VLAN.

matched_history: 2026-10-30 Legacy RADIUS Proxy to Virtual Proxy migration
uniqueness_check.rejected_near_match: This is a new selector/object architecture for devices without SNMP/CLI, not RADIUS proxy migration, FortiLink management credentials, or phone-specific VLAN refresh.

records.lesson_subject: Subscription VM license lifecycle: FDN entitlement refresh, 30-day validation loss and authentication shutdown
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator-VM subscription license retrieves entitlements from update.fortiguard.net over TCP/443; loss of entitlement validation for 30 days disables the license, lowers user limit to unlicensed VM limits and halts authentication while retaining administrator UI access.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: License file upload triggers reboot; active node retrieves subscription entitlements from FDN; HA pair requires separate subscription files and uses the lower entitlement if active/passive differ; periodic validation failure is logged with remaining grace-day messages.
records.failure_class: RADIUS/SAML/other authentication services stop while GUI remains reachable; license status appears disabled after FDN reachability loss; mixed perpetual/subscription HA pair or pre-8.0 subscription image causes migration/upgrade faults.
records.evidence_pattern: get system license-info shows local license; diagnose system updated status shows FDN-fetched entitlement; diagnose system updated info shows runtime update state; Logging > Log Access shows 4-hour/2-day/30-day validation countdown; verify TCP/443 to update.fortiguard.net.
records.remediation_path: Use FortiAuthenticator 8.0.0+; ensure DNS and outbound TCP/443 to update.fortiguard.net; install separate subscription licenses on both HA nodes; keep entitlement levels aligned; restore reachability before the 30-day validation window expires; do not apply subscription VM license to 6.6.7 before upgrading to 8.0.x.
records.question_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator GUI remains accessible but RADIUS and SAML both stop after a WAN outage; identify the subscription entitlement timer and the exact CLI evidence to distinguish license failure from authentication configuration.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator active/passive HA pair with separate subscription files, outbound TCP/443 entitlement path to FDN, shared authentication service consumers and 30-day validation timer leading to auth halt while admin GUI remains up.

uniqueness_check.rejected_near_match: This is VM subscription entitlement validation and service gating, not HA interface topology, FSSO identity filtering, or certificate lifecycle.

records.lesson_subject: Access Authentication: policy-level step-up gate for secret viewing and launch
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9 Access Authentication is an additional authentication gate independent of initial FortiPAM login, configurable at folder policy and overridable per secret, with remote-server choice, 0-180-minute duration and optional owner bypass.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User opens or launches a secret; policy/secret setting requires re-authentication; successful step-up creates a bounded access window reflected by Access Authentication Status; remote RADIUS/LDAP users may authenticate with FortiPAM login credentials for this step.
records.failure_class: User can sign in to FortiPAM but cannot view/edit/launch a protected secret; access window expires; owner bypass or per-secret override weakens inherited folder policy.
records.evidence_pattern: Inspect folder policy Access Authentication, secret Session Security override, selected remote server, duration and bypass; check Access Authentication Status remaining time and warning text on an unauthenticated secret.
records.remediation_path: Enable Access Authentication in the folder policy, set a suitable duration and server, leave owner bypass disabled unless explicitly approved, verify per-secret overrides, and test both secret editing and launcher execution for local and remote RADIUS/LDAP users.
records.question_fingerprint: A user has a valid FortiPAM session and launch permission but a protected secret refuses to open; identify the separate step-up transaction and its policy inheritance.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM login session branches to secret-folder policy and per-secret override, then step-up authentication to remote/local auth source, bounded access timer and separate edit/launch gates.

uniqueness_check.rejected_near_match: This is a second authentication gate at secret access time, not approval workflow, group membership, or session revocation.

records.lesson_subject: Incident Investigation Workspace: undirected incident/entity graph, timeline playback and contextual expansion
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM Analytics > Investigation creates an undirected graph rooted at an incident with host/IP, user, process and file entities; related incidents/entities can be recursively added and viewed in Force or Bipartite layout.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Load Incident ID -> query related entities and incidents from event database/CMDB/context -> graph nodes and edges are built -> timeline orders incident occurrences -> investigator expands entities, runs reports/reputation lookups, invokes connectors/playbooks, remediates or creates a case.
records.failure_class: Analyst treats a graph edge as causal proof, uses an incomplete time range, or cannot reconcile graph evidence with incident counts and backend PostgreSQL records.
records.evidence_pattern: Incident graph proves configured relationship/context, not causality; timeline proves temporal order; node sidebar and triggering events provide underlying evidence; backend phoenixdb queries validate incident existence/count/status but do not reproduce the graph's full relationship logic.
records.remediation_path: Start with root Incident ID and bounded time window; inspect triggering events and entity details; expand Related Incidents/Entities selectively; compare timeline order with raw events; use backend queries for count/status discrepancies; record conclusions in a case rather than treating graph proximity as proof.
records.question_fingerprint: An incident graph shows a user, host and two related incidents connected; determine which evidence establishes temporal order and which additional step is required before asserting causality.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Root incident node connected to host/IP, user, process and file entities; expanded related-incident nodes; a parallel timeline rail ordered by event time and a contextual evidence sidebar.

uniqueness_check.rejected_near_match: The investigation graph is analyst-driven incident/entity correlation, not the trained bipartite login-anomaly model or ML dataset/inference pipeline.

records.lesson_subject: Authenticated onboarding: SAML SP gate, invitation-code rotation and managed-endpoint migration
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSASE Management service becomes a SAML Service Provider and requires user authentication through an external IdP before a managed endpoint can register; enabling the feature generates a new invitation code and invalidates previously issued codes after migration.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Endpoint installer connects using invitation code -> management service redirects/authenticates through configured IdP -> SAML assertion returns to FortiSASE SP -> authenticated user/endpoint registration proceeds; existing endpoints are migrated and prompted to re-authenticate; EMM installers must be refreshed.
records.failure_class: Endpoint with a valid old invitation code is rejected or repeatedly re-prompts after activation; Entra group mapping fails when assertion exceeds 150 groups; preconfigured EMM installers retain stale invitation code.
records.evidence_pattern: Verify select-availability enablement, SAML Entity ID/ACS/SSO URL/certificate, user/group assignment, Domain identification claim, current invitation code, installer version and endpoint re-authentication/migration status.
records.remediation_path: Request FortiCare enablement; configure SAML SP/IdP metadata and signing certificate; use Include associated domain and username claim for Entra ID where required; filter groups to <=150 asserted memberships; redistribute updated installers and complete endpoint reboot/re-authentication before deleting legacy invitation code.
records.question_fingerprint: An endpoint has the correct old invitation code but cannot register after authenticated onboarding is enabled; identify the SAML gate, code rotation and migration sequence.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiClient endpoint and installer connect to FortiSASE Management SP, redirect to Entra ID/IdP, return signed SAML assertion, rotate invitation code, migrate existing endpoints and update EMM installer branch.

uniqueness_check.rejected_near_match: SCIM provisioning synchronizes directory lifecycle; this feature gates endpoint registration through SAML SP authentication and rotates the management invitation code.

records.lesson_subject: IPv6 segmentation over a shared SD-WAN/ADVPN overlay using VPN-ID/IPIP and per-VRF route separation
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 8.0 supports IPv6 over L3 VPN segmentation within one shared IPsec/ADVPN overlay; VPN-ID/IPIP encapsulation carries VRF identity so identical or overlapping tenant subnets remain isolated across hub/spokes.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Spoke classifies packet into local VRF -> multi-VRF IPsec encapsulation carries VPN ID -> hub/spoke decapsulates into matching VRF -> BGP exchanges VRF-specific routes and loopback IPv6 reachability via exchange-ip-addr6 -> ADVPN shortcut remains within same VRF.
records.failure_class: Cross-tenant route leakage or blackholing when VRF ID, VPN-ID encapsulation, BGP route-target/VRF import-export or IPv6 loopback exchange is inconsistent.
records.evidence_pattern: Validate VRF table membership and routes, IPsec phase1 encapsulation vpn-id-ipip, BGP neighbor/route exchange, exchange-ip-addr6 loopback reachability, VRF-aware health-check source/VRF and same-VRF versus cross-VRF ping tests.
records.remediation_path: Build consistent VRF IDs and route targets at hub/spokes; enable vpn-id-ipip on participating phase1 interfaces; exchange loopback IPv6 addresses; configure VRF-aware SD-WAN health checks; verify route import/export and shortcut formation separately for each VRF.
records.question_fingerprint: Two branches share one ADVPN overlay and use overlapping IPv6 prefixes for two departments; identify which encapsulation and route-exchange controls preserve same-VRF reachability without cross-VRF access.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Hub with one shared ADVPN overlay to two dual-VRF spokes; parallel VRF-A and VRF-B logical lanes carried by VPN-ID/IPIP, with IPv6 loopbacks/BGP and same-VRF shortcuts but no cross-VRF edges.

uniqueness_check.rejected_near_match: This is data-plane VRF isolation across a shared IPv6-capable overlay, not route leaking between VRFs or automated overlay provisioning.

records.lesson_subject: BGP conditional advertisement: multi-condition AND logic, exist/non-exist semantics, and cross-family IPv4/IPv6 RIB evaluation
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Neighbor-scoped conditional advertisement evaluates one or more condition route maps against BGP RIB; multiple maps are conjunctive; exist/non-exist gates advertisement; cross-family matching is disabled by default and controlled by cross-family-conditional-adv.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: BGP route learned/originated -> condition route-map match against BGP RIB -> AND evaluation -> advertise-map sent or suppressed to a specific neighbor; IPv4/IPv6 RIB selection changes when cross-family option is enabled.
records.failure_class: Route unexpectedly advertised or suppressed because condition route is absent from BGP RIB, route-map family mismatches, condition-type is inverted, or multiple conditions are not all satisfied.
records.evidence_pattern: get router info bgp neighbors; get router info bgp network; get router info6 routing-table bgp; neighbor Conditional advertise-map cond-state per map; diagnose ip router command show-vrf root show running router bgp.
records.remediation_path: Ensure condition prefixes are BGP-learned or BGP-originated; correct prefix/AS-path/route-map match; set exist or non-exist intentionally; enable cross-family-conditional-adv only when cross-family conditions are required; re-check neighbor advertised routes.
records.question_fingerprint: Given a dual-stack peer and two condition route maps with mixed address families, predict whether an advertised prefix is sent when one map is absent from the selected RIB and explain the cond-state output.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Dual-upstream FortiGate with primary/backup eBGP peers, IPv4 and IPv6 route-map condition nodes feeding an AND gate, per-neighbor advertise-map output; two RIB lanes and one cross-family toggle.

records.lesson_subject: FortiManager FCT_IPsec_Recommended template: activation, parameter binding, assignment scope, and installation
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Factory recommended FCT_IPsec_Recommended provisioning template is activated into an editable generated template using outgoing interface, IPv4 client range, netmask, and pre-shared key; resulting object is assigned to managed devices/groups and installed.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Factory template -> Activate and set parameters -> generated Activate_FCT_IPsec_Recommended object -> optional edit/clone/template-group -> device or device-group assignment -> install to FortiGate -> remote-access IPsec objects appear in device configuration.
records.failure_class: Template activation succeeds but the tunnel is absent from install preview or installation because the template is unassigned, generated interface is referenced by another object, or the device/group assignment scope is inconsistent.
records.evidence_pattern: FortiManager Provisioning Templates > IPsec Tunnel generated template, assigned devices/groups, install preview diff, install task log; FortiGate config vpn ipsec phase1-interface and phase2-interface plus interface/address object references.
records.remediation_path: Keep the template assigned to every target that consumes its generated interface; verify parameter values and address-object types; inspect interface references before deleting or replacing the template; preview and install after scope correction.
records.question_fingerprint: A FortiClient VPN template is activated and visible but the expected phase1 interface is missing from one target's install preview; identify the assignment/reference boundary to inspect before changing phase1 settings.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiManager template library -> activation parameter form -> generated template object -> assignment fan-out to two FortiGate devices -> install-preview/configuration boundary.

records.lesson_subject: FortiAnalyzer Fabric Supervisor HA: active-passive supervisor, delayed member reconnection, and supervisor data synchronization
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer Fabric Supervisor HA is active-passive only; Fabric Settings sync to secondary, but the secondary does not establish member connections until promoted; on failover members reconnect to the new primary and data sync follows.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Primary supervisor owns member control connections -> Fabric Settings replicate to secondary -> secondary remains disconnected from members -> primary failure/election -> secondary promoted -> members automatically reconnect -> data sync converges.
records.failure_class: Supervisor failover appears incomplete because the secondary is not expected to maintain member connections before promotion, supervisor data sync is incomplete, or preemption/role expectations cause unexpected primary re-election.
records.evidence_pattern: System Settings > HA Cluster Status and Supervisor Data Sync column; System Settings > Fabric Management > Fabric Settings topology on both nodes; member connection state before and after promotion; read-only/disabled member-management actions on secondary.
records.remediation_path: Use active-passive only; verify matching group credentials, peer identities and initial synchronization; wait for Supervisor Data Sync; validate member reconnection after promotion; account for preemption and upgrade behavior before forcing another failover.
records.question_fingerprint: A secondary supervisor shows the replicated Fabric topology but no direct member connections before failover; determine whether this is a fault or the documented standby boundary.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two supervisor nodes in active-passive pair above three Fabric members; primary has control-plane arrows to members, secondary receives configuration sync only; arrows switch after failover.

records.lesson_subject: FortiSwitch PoE power admission: dynamic guard band, AF/AT reservation, priority allocation, and FCFS precedence
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Dynamic guard band reserves expected device-class power before enabling a PoE port (AF 15.4 W, AT 36 W); power allocation can be priority-based or first-come-first-served; lower-numbered ports have higher priority and physical-port policy overrides global policy.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: PoE device detection/classification -> guard-band reservation -> available power admission check -> port power-on or denial; under priority mode higher-priority ports retain power and higher-numbered ports shed first; FCFS preserves already-powered endpoints.
records.failure_class: New endpoint remains unpowered despite a nominally available budget, or lower-priority ports lose power during a budget shortage because guard-band reservation and allocation mode are misunderstood.
records.evidence_pattern: Switch > Physical Ports PoE status/priority; per-port PoE state and allocated power; global versus physical-port allocation configuration; switch PoE budget and event/log evidence.
records.remediation_path: Check device class and AF/AT reservation, compare total available budget with guard-band reservations, verify global and per-port allocation modes, assign critical endpoints higher priority, and avoid connecting PoE PSE-to-PSE copper links without disabling PoE on both ports.
records.question_fingerprint: A new AT-powered AP does not turn on while lower-numbered critical devices remain active; infer the dynamic guard-band and port-priority behavior rather than treating it as an LLDP or VLAN fault.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSwitch PoE power-budget pool feeding per-port AF/AT guard-band reservations, priority queue tiers, and port power states; a separate global-versus-port override callout.

records.lesson_subject: Automated FortiAP location positioning: Static LoWi, GNSS priority, and 802.11mc RTT trilateration
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAP location source precedence is user-entered Static LoWi, then built-in GNSS, then LoWi calculation using IEEE 802.11mc RTT; trilateration requires at least four known-position responders plus one initiator; RTT measurement is configured on 5 GHz.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Known responder APs publish/serve known coordinates -> initiator sends 802.11mc RTT measurement requests -> distances to responders are collected -> 3D trilateration calculates position -> controller records lowi-pos-type and coordinate error bounds.
records.failure_class: Location is missing or inaccurate because no four usable responders exist, responder coordinates are unknown/uncertain, 802.11mc is disabled or configured on an unsupported band, or a higher-priority static/GNSS source masks calculated LoWi.
records.evidence_pattern: diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c wtp <serial> showing lowi-pos-type, latitude/longitude/altitude and error bounds; FortiAP rcfg/wcfg showing 802.11mc enabled and operational initiator/responder role.
records.remediation_path: Verify source precedence; establish at least four accurately positioned responders and one initiator; enable 802.11mc on 5 GHz; confirm operational role and coordinate uncertainty; clear or correct stale static position when automatic calculation is intended.
records.question_fingerprint: An initiator reports LoWi but its coordinate error remains large after deployment; identify responder count and known-coordinate quality as the limiting evidence, not RF client association.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Five-AP indoor floor plan: four fixed responder nodes with known XYZ coordinates around one initiator; RTT range circles intersect at 3D trilateration point; source-precedence stack Static > GNSS > LoWi.

records.lesson_subject: FortiNAC 9.4 Kerberos authentication through Local Winbind: domain join, keytab use, and identity boundary
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC 9.4 adds Kerberos support for user/admin authentication on FortiNAC-CA and admin authentication on FNAC-M; Local Winbind requires domain join and can use an uploaded Kerberos keytab instead of retaining a domain-join administrator password.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiNAC local Winbind configuration -> NetBIOS/domain/realm/DC selection -> AD domain join using credentials or keytab -> Winbind service identity material available -> Kerberos-enabled authentication path consumes the joined-domain context; LDAP directory remains a separate user/group synchronization path.
records.failure_class: Domain join reports misleading joined status or fails at AD discovery because NetBIOS name, Kerberos realm, DC hostname, time synchronization, keytab principal or directory type is wrong; non-AD LDAP/Kerberos services are incorrectly treated as AD join targets.
records.evidence_pattern: Winbind status and join logs; local Winbind configuration fields; domain controller discovery/join result; keytab principal and realm alignment; recent Community scenario shows FreeIPA is not an AD join target.
records.remediation_path: Use an AD-compatible domain join for Winbind; keep NetBIOS short name separate from DNS Kerberos realm; use a valid keytab principal where supported; align NTP with domain controllers; use LDAP-only integration for non-AD directories rather than attempting Samba AD join.
records.question_fingerprint: FortiNAC can query LDAP users but Winbind domain join fails against a FreeIPA server; determine which function requires AD join and which functions continue through LDAP.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC appliance with separate LDAP directory sync and Winbind/AD trust paths; keytab/credential input to domain join; Kerberos auth consumers; FreeIPA shown on LDAP-only path with no AD join arrow.

records.lesson_subject: FortiNAC-F isolation DNS proxy and Allowed Domains: captive redirection versus production DNS forwarding
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: In isolation VLANs, FortiNAC Service Network Interface (port2/eth1) is supplied as the client DNS server; unlisted domains resolve to the isolation interface/captive path, while Allowed Domains are proxied to configured production DNS servers; the appliance is not a router.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Isolated host receives DHCP with FortiNAC service-interface DNS -> sends DNS query to FortiNAC -> allowed-domain match -> forward query to production DNS -> return production answer; no match -> return isolation-interface address to preserve captive/registration flow.
records.failure_class: Isolated endpoint cannot reach update, certificate-validation, identity-provider or domain-controller endpoints because required FQDN/CNAME is not allowlisted, production DNS forwarding is wrong, or the FortiNAC FQDN/domain conflicts with the isolation DNS zone.
records.evidence_pattern: named.log PassThru entries grouped by queried domain; dig @<FortiNAC-port2-IP> <fqdn>; Allowed Domains list and production DNS IP; endpoint DNS answer; DHCP option showing FortiNAC service-interface DNS.
records.remediation_path: Identify failed names from named.log; add only required parent or exact domains and CNAME targets; configure reachable production DNS IPs; avoid wildcards and leading-dot names; do not add the FortiNAC FQDN's parent domain; flush client DNS and reconnect to isolation VLAN.
records.question_fingerprint: A quarantined endpoint receives an IP address but cannot validate an external identity-provider certificate; use the DNS query log and allowlist transaction to determine why the captive path is returned.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Isolation VLAN host -> FortiNAC port2 DNS proxy -> decision diamond Allowed Domains? -> production DNS forward/answer branch or captive isolation-IP branch; separate routed path to external service.

records.lesson_subject: TACACS+ post-auth authorization: privilege levels, shell-command argument controls, non-shell services, and cached authorization sessions
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: TACACS+ authorization objects define user/group rules, privilege level 0-15, non-shell service permissions and shell-command argument allow/deny lists; successful authentication creates an authorization session defaulting to 28,800 seconds, during which changed rules are not re-evaluated.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: TACACS+ authentication success -> authorization session established -> rule resolved from user/group -> service and shell command authorization request -> allowed command/arguments and privilege level returned -> subsequent command requests use session until expiry.
records.failure_class: Changed command permissions appear ineffective because an existing 8-hour authorization session retains prior policy, or command is denied because the shell-command object or argument match is incomplete.
records.evidence_pattern: Authentication > TACACS+ Service > Authorization rules/services/shell commands; TACACS+ authorization logs; session-duration policy value; request command and argument strings compared with allowed/denied argument sets.
records.remediation_path: Test with a fresh TACACS+ session or temporarily reduce the authorization-session duration to 120-36000 seconds; scope rules to user/group; define explicit default permissions; validate exact command and argument strings; restore intended session duration after testing.
records.question_fingerprint: A TACACS+ user keeps executing a command that was removed from the allowed set minutes ago; identify the authorization-session cache lifetime rather than changing the client match policy.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Network device -> FortiAuthenticator authentication -> cached authorization-session object -> group/user rule -> service and shell-command argument decision -> permit/deny response.

records.lesson_subject: FortiPAM Web-API password changer: CSRF token extraction, nested JSON parsing, response expectations, and branchable changer sequences
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Web-API password changer executes ordered HTTP requests; Expect steps validate status/body and can extract cookies or tokens from headers/body/cookies; CSRF cookie extraction stores $CSRFTOKEN; multi-layer JSON response parsing supports nested response fields; Expect can branch to a command number.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Authenticate to target API -> capture session cookie/CSRF token -> submit password-change request with extracted token and new secret -> parse nested JSON/status response -> branch or continue -> verifier confirms the target accepted the new credential before FortiPAM marks change successful.
records.failure_class: Password rotation reports HTTP 400 or false success because CSRF token was not extracted or replayed, JSON response nesting is parsed incorrectly, or the verifier accepts a response that does not prove credential change.
records.evidence_pattern: FortiPAM changer step execution and HTTP status/body; extracted token location/key; cookie/header values; response-body match; command-step sequence and verifier result; WAD password-changer debug categories when needed.
records.remediation_path: Separate Execute and Expect steps; extract CSRF token from the correct response location and key; reference $CSRFTOKEN in the subsequent request; parse the correct nested JSON path; require explicit success code/body; verify by authenticating with the new credential.
records.question_fingerprint: A Web-API password changer authenticates and receives HTTP 200, but the password remains unchanged; determine which token-extraction or response-verification boundary is missing.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM changer state machine with HTTP Execute -> HTTP Expect/token extraction -> HTTP Execute/password update -> HTTP Expect/branch decision -> independent verifier; token/cookie feedback arrow.

records.lesson_subject: FortiSIEM Visual Report Designer: template scope precedence, PDF layout objects, upgrade migration, and report-folder limitation
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Visual PDF Report Designer builds templates from cover page, table of contents, sections/pages, text/images/charts/report tables/attachments; report-specific template overrides folder template, which overrides root system template; Service Provider templates are Super/Global scoped.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Create/edit template at report, folder, or bundle scope -> save template assignment -> report generation resolves most-specific applicable template -> PDF rendering; first login after 7.0 upgrade migrates pre-7.0 templates and normalizes multi-chart layout.
records.failure_class: Custom PDF design is not applied because a higher-precedence report template overrides folder/root template, or first-login migration stalls because unsupported custom folder templates remain; old subsections are not supported.
records.evidence_pattern: Resources > Reports Report Design Template column; report/folder/bundle assignment; PDF Preview; migration error 'Another User is updating all Report Templates on this machine'; exported PDF page/section layout.
records.remediation_path: Inspect template assignment at report, folder, and root scopes; remove custom templates from folders before upgrade; retain supported report- and bundle-level templates; preview generated PDF and reassign at the correct scope.
records.question_fingerprint: A report bundle renders with the default design despite a custom folder template, and an upgrade migration reports another user updating templates; determine precedence and unsupported folder-template migration boundary.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Three-level template precedence stack (report > folder > root) feeding PDF renderer; side panel for cover/TOC/sections/objects; upgrade migration path with unsupported folder-template branch.

records.lesson_subject: FortiSASE DNS Filter: local-domain precedence, FortiGuard fallback, DNS translation, captive-portal exception, and rating-error fail-open
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: DNS Filter evaluates local domain filters before FortiGuard category rating; local allow bypasses category evaluation, monitor continues to FortiGuard, block redirects; DNS translation rewrites returned IP; rating-error option can fail open; edge captive portal requires DNS support exception.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client DNS query -> local domain filter match/action -> if no local terminal action, FortiGuard rating -> allow/monitor/block portal -> optional DNS translation of resolved IP -> DNS response and DNS Filter log.
records.failure_class: An allowed domain still fails because its authoritative DNS server hostname is independently blocked; DNS translation returns wrong address due to mask; edge captive portal SSO fails because captive-dns-exempt policy lacks DNS Filter or Edge device captive portal support.
records.evidence_pattern: Operations > Logs > Security > DNS Filter query/response entries; local domain rule action and category action; FortiGuard rating error log; DNS answer before/after translation; captive-dns-exempt policy profile group.
records.remediation_path: Allow the delegated authoritative nameserver domain as well as the requested domain; verify local allow/monitor/block precedence; validate original/translated IP and mask; configure edge DNS exemption and captive-portal support; decide explicitly whether rating failure should fail open.
records.question_fingerprint: A domain is locally allowed but still fails resolution because its NS hostnames fall into a blocked FortiGuard category; identify the independent DNS queries and policy precedence.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Client resolver -> local domain filter decision -> FortiGuard category-rating branch -> block portal/allow/monitor; optional DNS translation stage; edge captive DNS exemption side path.

records.lesson_subject: ADVPN shortcut recovery hold-down: low-priority reintegration, service-strategy selection, and SLA-mode boundary
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: When an ADVPN shortcut or primary hub-spoke VPN recovers, the SD-WAN service can keep that member at low priority until hold-down-time expires; default is zero and valid range is 0-10000000 seconds; hold-down is tied to service-strategy behavior and is not a universal SLA-mode delay.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Tunnel fails -> member removed/less preferred -> tunnel recovers -> shortcut re-enters service candidate set at low priority -> hold-down timer runs -> member returns to normal strategy ranking after expiry.
records.failure_class: Recovered shortcut immediately attracts traffic and flaps, or operator expects hold-down to delay SLA-mode failback when the documented strategy does not apply; wrong service mode is diagnosed as tunnel instability.
records.evidence_pattern: diagnose sys sdwan service4/service output showing Hold down time, Hold start, current time, member alive/selected state; tunnel status and Performance SLA state; config system sdwan config service set hold-down-time.
records.remediation_path: Confirm service strategy and feature applicability; set a measured hold-down value on the relevant service; compare member selection before and after expiry; do not expect the timer to solve failed SLA measurements or apply where the mode does not support it.
records.question_fingerprint: An ADVPN shortcut repeatedly becomes preferred immediately after recovery, but the service uses an SLA strategy; determine whether the configured hold-down timer is applicable before tuning its value.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Hub-and-spoke with primary and shortcut tunnels; failure removes shortcut, recovery reinserts it into low-priority quarantine timer, then strategy ranking resumes; separate SLA-mode applicability callout.

records.lesson_subject: Enhanced multicast session identity for wildcard-VLAN virtual wire pairs
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: For wildcard-VLAN VWP multicast, the session identity incorporates ingress interface and VLAN ID so identical source/group/protocol traffic in separate VLAN contexts is represented by separate multicast sessions.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Packet enters VWP member -> VLAN context is preserved -> multicast policy lookup -> session keyed with ingress interface and VLAN -> forwarding/NPU path; repeated source/group on another VLAN creates a separate session.
records.failure_class: Cross-VLAN multicast session aliasing or VLAN-context loss; wildcard VLAN/filter/policy mismatch.
records.evidence_pattern: diagnose sys mcast-session list shows distinct session IDs and different indev/vlanid for same source/group; policy/path counters and VLAN-aware packet capture correlate the result.
records.remediation_path: Enable wildcard-vlan on the VWP, set the intended vlan-filter, verify multicast policy ingress/egress and tagged VLAN handling, then confirm separate sessions; do not infer policy success from a single session or a capture on the wrong interface.
records.question_fingerprint: Same source and multicast group arriving on VLAN 50 and VLAN 60 must create separate sessions because ingress interface and VLAN are part of the VWP multicast key.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: One VWP spanning two tagged VLAN paths; same multicast source/group on both; two independent session-table rows annotated with indev and vlanid.
records.uniqueness_assessment: No prior 30-day lesson teaches VWP multicast session-key composition; prior multicast lessons cover TTL, PIM/BSR, and shapers, not VLAN-aware session identity.

records.lesson_subject: Authenticated NTPv4 time synchronization with SHA-256 keys
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager 8.0 NTP client authenticates NTPv4 server exchanges with SHA-256 using a shared key, key identifier, and explicit hex/ASCII key format.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Chrony serves NTP and loads its keyfile -> FortiManager selects server, authentication, SHA-256, key format, key and key-id -> authenticated time exchange -> diagnose system ntp status reports server state.
records.failure_class: Time server reachable but authentication fails because key ID, algorithm, format, or secret differs; clock remains unsynchronized.
records.evidence_pattern: Chrony keyfile entry, FortiManager ntpserver object, and diagnose system ntp status; compare key ID and key material without exposing secrets.
records.remediation_path: Match key-id, SHA256 algorithm, hex/ASCII format and exact shared key on both sides; ensure Chrony allows the FortiManager source and keyfile is loaded; verify status and clock offset.
records.question_fingerprint: A reachable Chrony server rejects FortiManager NTP authentication; align the key ID and SHA-256 key format/material rather than changing routing.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiManager client -> routed management network -> Chrony NTP server; SHA-256 key-ID exchange shown separately from UDP reachability; status verification below.
records.uniqueness_assessment: No previous 30-day FortiManager lesson covers NTP authentication or time-source integrity; prior topics cover device workflows, templates, and control-plane features.

records.lesson_subject: Layer-3 geo-redundant active-active FortiAnalyzer HA
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer active-active geo HA allows members in separate routed data centers to receive logs from directly connected devices and forward those logs/archive files to peers and remote servers; unicast heartbeat removes the Layer-2 VIP dependency.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Two FAZ nodes configure a-a mode and peer identity -> unicast heartbeat over routed WAN -> initial sync/election -> each member ingests local device logs -> peer/remote forwarding -> FortiGate primary/alternate server failover/fallback.
records.failure_class: Cluster stuck at initial sync, peer heartbeat blocked, VRRP filtered, or one site silently lacks log ingestion/remote forwarding.
records.evidence_pattern: diagnose ha status shows role, peer, initial log sync and configuration sync; packet capture for IP protocol 112; FortiGate server/alt-server/fallback config; per-node log receipt and remote forwarding.
records.remediation_path: Disable initial-sync on at least one node during initial formation; enable unicast; permit VRRP protocol 112; omit cluster VIP across L3 sites and use heartbeat interface; configure primary/alternate FAZ and validate ingestion from devices at both sites.
records.question_fingerprint: Two data centers have only routed connectivity and both must ingest/forward local logs; choose active-active geo HA with unicast heartbeat and no L2 VIP.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two geographically separated data centers joined by routed WAN; each FAZ node has local FortiGate log sources; unicast heartbeat and peer log/archive forwarding; optional remote log server.
records.uniqueness_assessment: Prior FortiAnalyzer coverage includes active-passive Fabric Supervisor HA; this lesson is a distinct active-active data-plane/log-ingestion architecture across Layer 3 sites.

records.lesson_subject: DCBX negotiation, ETS priority groups, and priority-based flow control
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitchOS 8.0 DCBX exchanges ETS configuration/recommendation, PFC configuration, and application-priority TLVs via LLDP; ETS maps CoS queues to priority groups with guaranteed bandwidth; PFC pauses selected priorities.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Ingress 802.1p CoS -> trusted Dot1p map -> egress queue -> ETS priority group -> scheduler guarantees bandwidth; LLDP DCBX advertises application priority/PFC/ETS to peer; peer negotiates compatible lossless classes.
records.failure_class: Lossless RoCE/FCoE/iSCSI traffic drops or starves because queue mapping, DCBX TLVs, peer configuration, PFC priorities, or ETS bandwidth allocation disagree.
records.evidence_pattern: Supported model and FortiSwitchOS version; LLDP profile contains app-prio/ets-config/ets-rec/pfc-config; trust-dot1p-map enabled; DCBX enabled on both peers; priority-group rates total 100%; per-priority PFC settings.
records.remediation_path: Confirm eligible hardware; use Dot1p trust (not simultaneous DSCP trust on the same DCBX interface); configure DCBX on both peers; map CoS queues to PGs; separate PFC-enabled, lossy, and strict-priority groups; make ETS rates sum to 100%.
records.question_fingerprint: RoCE needs lossless behavior only for its selected priority; solve by matching DCBX app-priority, queue-to-PG mapping and PFC on both peers, not global pause on all traffic.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSwitch-to-peer Ethernet link with LLDP DCBX TLV exchange; ingress CoS map -> queues -> three ETS groups (lossy/lossless/strict) -> PFC pause on lossless priority.
records.uniqueness_assessment: No prior 30-day FortiSwitch lesson covers DCBX, ETS, PFC, or lossless Ethernet; previous topics cover MACsec, STP, PTP, mirroring, and PoE.

records.lesson_subject: Dynamic captive-portal redirect URLs from RADIUS Access-Accept
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS WiFi controller reads the Fortinet-Captive-Portal-URL RADIUS attribute (vendor attribute 27) from Access-Accept and redirects the wireless client to a session-specific portal when dynamic redirect is enabled on a tunnel-mode auth-mac captive-portal VAP.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client associates to captive-portal SSID -> MAC-auth RADIUS request -> policy engine returns Access-Accept with Fortinet-Captive-Portal-URL -> FortiGate controller applies redirect -> browser opens the returned session-specific portal.
records.failure_class: Client lands on default/static portal or no redirect because VAP mode/type is wrong, feature disabled, or Access-Accept lacks/contains malformed attribute 27.
records.evidence_pattern: VAP CLI shows captive-portal enable, portal-type auth-mac, captive-portal-dynamic-redirect-url enable; RADIUS trace shows Access-Accept and vendor attribute 27; browser redirect URL matches policy response.
records.remediation_path: Use tunnel-mode captive portal with auth-mac; enable dynamic redirect; confirm RADIUS server/group mapping and Access-Accept attribute 27 value; test authorized and unauthorized policy outcomes separately.
records.question_fingerprint: A session-specific portal URL is supplied in the RADIUS Access-Accept; enable dynamic redirect on a tunnel-mode auth-mac VAP and return Fortinet-Captive-Portal-URL attribute 27.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Wireless client/AP -> FortiGate WiFi controller -> RADIUS policy engine; Access-Accept carries attribute 27 back to controller; browser redirect to session-specific portal.
records.uniqueness_assessment: No previous 30-day FortiAP lesson covers RADIUS-supplied dynamic portal URLs; prior portal content concerns other captive-portal controls and does not teach attribute-27 redirect selection.

records.lesson_subject: RADIUS identity normalization and LDAP domain matching for user-to-policy resolution
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC parses qualified usernames into user/domain components, applies exact configured domain matching, resolves directory identity and maps directory records to local user IDs; anonymous outer identity or a mismatched domain format can prevent LDAP group/user matching.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Endpoint sends RADIUS identity -> FortiNAC records the presented username -> parser separates user/domain -> directory selection and LDAP lookup -> local user record/user ID is matched -> user/host profile and access policy can consume identity.
records.failure_class: Authentication succeeds at RADIUS but LDAP-backed policy does not match because the visible username is anonymous, domain format is inconsistent, or multiple directories contain duplicate IDs.
records.evidence_pattern: Network > RADIUS log shows username; Directory Domain Name setting; compare user, user@domain, domain\\user formats; directory synchronization and user ID record; resulting policy/user mapping.
records.remediation_path: Inspect the exact identity received; verify endpoint identity privacy behavior; make the login format and exact domain configuration consistent; remove an unintended Domain Name requirement or configure the expected UPN format; use unique LDAP identifier mappings across multiple directories.
records.question_fingerprint: RADIUS log says anonymous and LDAP group policy misses; first inspect the identity sent and FortiNAC's exact domain parsing/format rules, not password validity.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Endpoint -> RADIUS identity -> FortiNAC username/domain parser -> one or more LDAP directories -> local user record -> policy/profile; anonymous identity and domain mismatch shown as branch failures.
records.uniqueness_assessment: Prior FortiNAC lessons cover RADIUS event export, dashboards, role precedence and policy order; none covers username canonicalization, EAP identity privacy, or exact LDAP domain matching.

records.lesson_subject: Local RADIUS EAP-TLS certificate revocation is OCSP-only
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F Local RADIUS validates EAP-TLS client certificate chains using RADIUS Endpoint Trust [radius] and supports OCSP revocation checks; the Local RADIUS path has no CRL/CDP lookup/import option.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client presents certificate in EAP-TLS -> FortiNAC validates chain against RADIUS Endpoint Trust [radius] -> reads OCSP URL from certificate AIA -> queries responder -> accepts/rejects according to status; HA control node must reach responder and have trust chain.
records.failure_class: CDP-only certificate fails when OCSP is enabled; root/intermediate missing; OCSP URL absent/unreachable; failover node lacks applicable trust chain.
records.evidence_pattern: openssl x509 output for Authority Information Access and CRL Distribution Points; Local Service OCSP setting; RADIUS Endpoint Trust [radius] target; RADIUS logs and good/revoked test certificates.
records.remediation_path: Publish OCSP and include AIA OCSP URL in reissued certificates; upload all issuing roots/intermediates to RADIUS Endpoint Trust [radius] for both HA nodes; verify DNS/HTTP reachability; if CRL is mandatory, terminate EAP-TLS on an external CRL-capable RADIUS server and proxy from FortiNAC-F.
records.question_fingerprint: A client certificate contains CDP but no OCSP URL; Local RADIUS cannot use CDP/CRL, so issue an OCSP-enabled certificate or use an external CRL-capable RADIUS server.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: EAP-TLS endpoint certificate -> FortiNAC-F Local RADIUS -> trusted CA chain + AIA OCSP URL -> OCSP responder; separate unsupported CDP/CRL path marked unavailable; HA peer reachability.
records.uniqueness_assessment: No previous 30-day FortiNAC-F lesson covers local RADIUS certificate revocation. FortiAuthenticator CRL handling is a different product workflow and is not reused.

records.lesson_subject: TACACS+ client groups as reusable policy targets and REST-managed objects
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.2 adds TACACS+ client group objects; policies can select individual clients and/or groups; REST API exposes client-group and group-client association resources.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Network device source IP matches TACACS+ client object -> membership/group association is evaluated -> policy targeting client or group applies -> configured identity source authenticates operator -> TACACS+ response/authorization returned.
records.failure_class: New network device is not matched by any policy because it is absent from the group or group is not selected in the policy; duplicated individual and group policy targets can create unexpected policy coverage.
records.evidence_pattern: Authentication > TACACS+ Service > Clients > Group membership; policy Chosen TACACS+ Client Groups; REST resources /tacplusclientgroups/ and /tacplusgroupclient/; TACACS request source IP.
records.remediation_path: Create or import client group, add the exact device client objects, attach group to intended TACACS+ policy, verify source address/NAT, and test authentication/authorization from a member device.
records.question_fingerprint: Hundreds of routers need one TACACS policy without selecting each one individually; create a TACACS+ client group and bind that group to the policy.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Many routers/switches -> TACACS+ client objects -> reusable client group -> policy -> identity source -> TACACS+ response; REST API shown as management plane.
records.uniqueness_assessment: No previous 30-day FortiAuthenticator lesson covers TACACS+ client-group abstraction or its REST associations; prior lessons cover TACACS authorization and HA/licensing.

records.lesson_subject: Reusable Guest Instruction Profiles attached to secrets
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9 Guest Instruction profiles are reusable formatted guidance objects independent of secret objects; optional image/video resources use a separate instruction-resource allocation and profiles are attached to secrets.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Enable Guest Instruction Feature -> allocate instruction resources if media is used -> create reusable profile and resources -> attach profile in a secret's Settings -> guest checks out secret -> attached instructions render with the secret.
records.failure_class: Guest sees no instructions because feature is disabled, profile not attached, resource allocation is zero for media, or resource reference is missing.
records.evidence_pattern: System > Settings > Advanced toggle and Instruction Resources Allocation (%); Secret Settings > Instruction Profile list; resource library; secret Settings > Guest Instruction assignment; guest checkout view.
records.remediation_path: Enable feature, set resource allocation above zero when media is needed, create profile/resources, attach profile to each intended secret, and validate using a guest checkout account; replace shared resource carefully because references update.
records.question_fingerprint: Reusable operational guidance must appear when a guest checks out several secrets; create one instruction profile and attach it to each secret, without confusing it with access policy or credentials.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Instruction resource library -> reusable instruction profile -> multiple secret objects -> guest checkout screen; credentials/access policy shown as separate control plane.
records.uniqueness_assessment: No previous 30-day FortiPAM lesson covers guest instruction profiles or resource reuse; prior PAM lessons cover gateways, RDP, backups and JIT.

records.lesson_subject: Dynamic IP watchlists populated by username-to-IP lookup
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM rule action LookupIpByUser populates an IP-based watchlist from the Identity and Location database even when the triggering event has username but no IP attribute; it removes stale IP when another user takes it and updates when the user changes IP.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Rule fires with username -> Step 3 Define Action -> Watch List Edit -> LookupIpByUser -> identity/location database resolves current IP -> IP watchlist add/update/remove -> downstream rule/remediation consumes current address.
records.failure_class: Empty or stale watchlist due missing/stale user-IP mapping, identity collection gap, or incorrect rule action configuration.
records.evidence_pattern: Rule action shows LookupIpByUser; Identity and Location database maps username to current IP; watchlist entry appears, changes on user IP change, and is removed on IP reassignment.
records.remediation_path: Verify identity/location data freshness and user mapping; configure LookupIpByUser in the rule's Watch List Edit action; test user address change and reassignment before enabling automatic blocking.
records.question_fingerprint: A rule event has username but no IP; use LookupIpByUser to resolve the current IP from Identity and Location and maintain the IP watchlist.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Username-only event -> FortiSIEM rule -> Identity & Location user-IP mapping -> LookupIpByUser -> dynamic IP watchlist -> downstream response.
records.uniqueness_assessment: No previous 30-day FortiSIEM lesson covers dynamic watchlist enrichment or user-to-IP mapping; prior lessons cover investigation graphs, ML workbench and query functions.

records.lesson_subject: Source IP anchoring for user/group- and country-specific egress NAT
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSASE source IP anchoring maps remote-user source criteria (user/group or country) at a security PoP to a dedicated public IP used for source NAT; implementation creates a policy route and firewall policy on the PoP FortiGate.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Remote user enters security PoP -> source criteria matches user/group or country -> policy route selects anchor -> firewall policy SNATs to dedicated public IP -> destination sees deterministic customer egress IP.
records.failure_class: Wrong or shared egress IP, missing anchor/entitlement, unmatched group/country, or third-party geolocation feed has not propagated.
records.evidence_pattern: IP Management > Security Public IPs > IP anchors, source criteria, PoP mapping, dedicated IP allocation/licensing, test egress IP from matched and unmatched users, public IP feed/geolocation.
records.remediation_path: Open FortiCare request for backend deployment; confirm license and additional IP allocation; map user group/country to PoP anchor; validate policy route/SNAT and external allowlist; allow third-party geolocation propagation time.
records.question_fingerprint: A remote user group must always egress from a dedicated address at a PoP; use source IP anchoring and a user/group criterion, not merely geolocation metadata.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Remote user/agent -> FortiSASE PoP -> group/country match -> policy route + SNAT -> dedicated public IP -> SaaS/private destination; unanchored default path shown separately.
records.uniqueness_assessment: No previous 30-day FortiSASE lesson covers source IP anchoring; prior topics cover DNS, tunnel readiness, IPAM control-plane subnet and DEM.

records.lesson_subject: Session-affine SD-WAN load balancing using source-IP and source-destination-IP hash modes
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: SD-WAN load-balance hash-mode selects member by round-robin, source IP, source-destination IP, session weight, or measured volume; source-based hashes preserve egress-member affinity for a client or client/destination pair.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Flow matches explicit/implicit SD-WAN rule -> manual or SLA strategy selects eligible members -> hash-mode maps flow to member -> firewall session/NAT uses selected underlay -> subsequent same-key flows retain intended member affinity.
